Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme
